## Objective

The initial implementation will establish a safe, usable diabetes-team workflow: blood-taking first, then a follow-up consultation once results are available. It will also establish a trusted diabetes cohort, structured recall, a repeating Table 2 history of contact/residence/vital/follow-up status, and the data needed for reporting key diabetes metrics.

## Patient pathway

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  A["<b>Blood-taking visit</b><br/><small>From 1 September 2026</small>"]
  B["<b>Results reviewed</b><br/>"]
  C["<b>Follow-up consultation</b><br/><small>From mid-September 2026</small>"]
  D["<b>Database updated</b>"]

  A --> B --> C --> D
```

At the blood-taking visit, the team confirms the patient identity. On return of results, staff verify the patient-result match and enter only accepted results in Table 5. The follow-up consultation records the clinical review, physical measurements, medicines, lifestyle/preventive care, foot and eye status, and planned actions.

## Delivery timetable

| Period | Focus | Main work | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 July--31 August 2026 | Readiness | Confirm core data set, diagnosis-confirmation and active-resident rules, Table 2 status-history structure, default/re-engagement and migration rules, access roles, local laboratory identity/acceptance procedure, and first reporting rules. Build and test REDCap instruments. Undertake laboratory, pharmacy and diabetes-workflow walkthroughs. | Signed-off MVP specification, tested build and local operating procedures |
| 1--14 September 2026 | Start blood-taking | Begin planned blood-taking visits; confirm identifiers; record ASET/request identifiers and specimen dates; enter accepted historical results only where confidently linked. | First live blood-taking cohort and laboratory tracking list |
| From mid-September 2026 | Start consultations | Begin consultations after approximately two-week result turnaround. Complete diagnosis review, physical review, medicine review and priority actions. | First complete two-contact patient journeys |
| October 2026 | Controlled scale-up | Prioritise people not seen for years, people without recent HbA1c, unconfirmed/probable cases, and people with known high-risk markers. Review workflow bottlenecks weekly. | Prioritised recall list and workflow issue log |
| November--December 2026 | Embed routine care | Expand the blood-taking/consultation cycle, complete foot and eye recording/referral processes, review missingness and audit a sample of record linkages. | Stable six-monthly review workflow and early coverage dashboard |
| January 2027 | First implementation review | Produce the first five-month internal report; assess data completeness, denominator confidence, care coverage, demand, and corrective actions. | Internal registry implementation report and action plan |

No numerical throughput target is specified until clinic, laboratory and follow-up consultation capacity is agreed. The initial target should be a safe, complete pathway for each patient, not rapid coverage at the expense of matching and review quality.

## Priorities and accountable decisions

| Priority | Required decision or task | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted cohort | Agree the minimum evidence for confirmed diabetes and the handling of probable, high-risk, excluded, duplicate and non-resident records. | Defines M01, M02, M20 and all active-care denominators. |
| Patient identity | Agree the identifiers checked at blood-taking and the procedure for uncertain or mismatched results. | Reduces wrong-patient laboratory risk. |
| Two-contact workflow | Agree responsibility, appointment method and escalation route between blood-taking and consultation. | Makes the intended patient journey deliverable. |
| Core data set | Confirm which Core fields are completed at blood-taking, consultation and separate foot/eye contacts. | Limits staff burden and prevents incomplete forms. |
| Recall and action | Agree priority criteria, six-month review due dates, potential/definite default rules, tracing actions, re-engagement, and management of people temporarily overseas or transferred to another provider. | Makes the registry an active care tool without misclassifying known migration or medical travel as default. |
| Reporting | Approve the SAP’s denominators, time windows and first reporting date. | Produces interpretable M01--M26 outputs. |

## Role-based workflow

| Role | Core responsibility |
|---|---|
| Diabetes clinician | Diagnosis confirmation, clinical review rules, escalation and clinical sign-off |
| Diabetes/community nursing team | Blood-taking and consultation workflow, recall, Core data entry and action follow-up |
| Laboratory lead | Local request/identifier process, result turnaround and resolution of matching queries |
| Pharmacy lead | Medication-review workflow and agreed medication ontology |
| Registry/data lead | REDCap configuration, user rights, quality checks, data extracts, SAP implementation and reporting |
| Public health lead | Governance, delivery oversight, use of reports and resourcing decisions |

## Readiness checklist

- [ ] Diagnosis-confirmation and active-resident denominator rules agreed.
- [ ] Repeating Table 2 status-history instrument configured, including address, residence/migration, vital status and follow-up fields.
- [ ] Potential default, definite default, tracing, re-engagement and reason-for-follow-up-gap rules agreed.
- [ ] Blood-taking identity and ASET/request recording procedure tested.
- [ ] Table 5 acceptance status and result-entry procedure tested.
- [ ] Consultation instruments tested with a realistic patient scenario.
- [ ] Restricted access to Table 2 configured and reviewed.
- [ ] Recall list and priority categories agreed.
- [ ] Medication classes and ACE-I/ARB/antihypertensive flags agreed.
- [ ] Foot and eye referral pathways and due-date fields agreed.
- [ ] First internal reporting date and review meeting scheduled.

## Early measures of implementation success

At the January 2027 review, report the number of people entered, classification status, blood-taking contacts, accepted laboratory-result bundles, consultations completed, current residence/migration status, potential and definite defaults, re-engagements, and people with unresolved identity or data-quality queries. Interpret M01--M26 cautiously during this establishment phase: early values will principally show coverage and backlog rather than stable island-wide care performance.
